rubrics.evidence: The step instruction names the package, API surface, normalization and ownership rules, JSON shapes, CLI results, fixture contracts, documentation, and installation changes. These are sufficient to implement the intended feature from the clean CPython checkout without the review-only reference files.

HarnessTests.test_scripts_use_no_network copies only gen_fixtures.sh and verify_offline.sh into a temporary Tools tree; tests/probe.py:harness_scripts_use_no_network repeats this assumption. The instruction requires offline scripts but never requires them to be self-contained or to work after sibling helper files are removed.

The sole recorded attempt fails exactly this unstated relocation condition: its copied shell script cannot find its sibling _fixtures.py. There is no cross-model sample to establish a broader pattern, but the available failure is explained by an undocumented grading requirement rather than a mistaken implementation.

The specification defines behavior rather than an implementation recipe. A solver must design consistent grant lifecycle, overlap detection, repository metadata, upload authorization, persistence, policy evaluation, and CPython build integration.

The reference and grading files were not exposed in the solving checkout, but the separate verifier runs submitted code as root and copies /tests without a user or read-only boundary. Submitted package initialization can overwrite /tests/parser.py and /tests/probe.py before they execute; a disposable reproduction using copied verifier files and the unchanged reward-computation block accepted a package with no GrantStore at reward 1.

The required package-root export GrandfatheredRegistry is not checked: deleting its root import and __all__ entry from the reference still passed all 109 feature tests runnable without rebuilding and all 43 applicable probe checks. The two excluded probe checks concern interpreter installation and unittest integrity, so neither checks this missing export; documentation checks also miss the reference's invalid NEWS filename.

Both scoring channels remain writable by the submitted code they execute, despite source hashing and child-process attestation. In a scratch demonstration, an API-free package rewrote copies of parser.py and probe.py, read the required IDs from config.json at execution time, and made the original final reward calculation accept 451/451 fabricated passes; no supplied trial performed this attack.

The model's legitimate decomposition into two shell entrypoints plus _fixtures.py is rejected by the two-file copy in both the unittest and probe. I reproduced the sole failure, then made the same network test pass by copying the whole Tools/packagenamespaces directory before appending the comments, without changing the submission.

tree_manifest.json hashes 97 Python/*.o build products, including Python/sysmodule.o, while run_script.sh rebuilds them after the permitted stdlib header change. A second grade of the same solved tree therefore fails integrity against the old object hash; build/DECISIONS.md records this exact repeat-run failure, although fresh one-shot grading completed normally in the supplied trial.

The 111 fail-to-pass cases require the absent package, new scripts, new documentation references, or new installation registration. Their guarded imports and explicit file/content assertions fail on the unmodified checkout; build/DECISIONS.md also records zero passing feature IDs and 340/340 passing regression IDs on the base.

Verification is automated and CPU-only: the recorded verifier completed in approximately 106 seconds, with the ten-module test run itself taking 6.2 seconds. This is substantially cheaper than implementing and validating the package and requires no human judgment or external service.

The reference adds Misc/NEWS.d/next/Library/2026-11-04-12-00-00.pep-752.ss007.rst, whose pep-752 filename field is invalid for CPython's blurb tool. Validating that exact name with blurb raised AssertionError: Found unparsable field in 'next' filename: 'pep-752'; normal Doc/Makefile documentation builds invoke blurb merge, so the documentation integration is broken despite the keyword-only NEWS test passing.

No oracle trial directory is supplied; build/DECISIONS.md records successful fresh-container oracle grading with reward 1.0. My extracted-reference run passed all 109 feature tests that do not require a rebuilt interpreter, and the NEWS defect lies outside the shipped grader's checks; repeat-run object hashing is addressed under R09:Test reliability.

Namespace authorization is useful packaging functionality, but adding this complete repository and installer model to CPython is a synthetic feature request rather than a natural implementation site for repository policy. PEP 752 does not itself establish this new standard-library API, and the instruction supplies its own unusually extensive contract.

The work combines packaging name normalization and namespace ownership with CPython's generated standard-library module list, installation rules, regrtest, and documentation conventions. The trajectory had to investigate and validate these project-specific mechanisms.

The fixtures are small synthetic unit-test examples, but their grant records, project-owner mappings, exemptions, and independent repository reproduce the relevant real data relationships. No requirement depends on realistic repository scale or performance.

The recorded zero reward comes from lost script dependencies in a hidden test, after the implementation satisfied the specified behaviors and installation checks. The trajectory also spent effort recovering from interpreter rebuild crashes, so this observed reward does not distinguish the substantive implementation capabilities the task intends to measure.
